Severe Storms Damage Spanish Banking Offices, Disrupting Operations

Madrid, Spain — A series of severe storms has battered the Spanish banking industry’s own facilities this week, causing widespread disruption across the sector’s branches, offices and data centers. Heavy rainfall and flooding, particularly in the Madrid and Valencia regions, have inundated ground-floor banking premises, forcing several firms to suspend in-person services and temporarily close affected locations.

The storms, which began late Monday and intensified overnight, have left multiple banking sites without power or with water damage. Santander Nacional, one of Spain’s largest retail banks, reported that more than 30 of its sites have been impacted, with employees evacuated from five offices in central Madrid due to flooding. “Our priority is the safety of our staff and the security of our clients’ assets,” said spokesperson Lucia Herrero. “We are working to restore normal operations as quickly as possible.”

Other banking groups, including Banco Popular Hispano and Iberica Financiera, also reported extensive disruptions. A spokesperson for Banco Popular Hispano stated that at least 18 of its branches in the Valencia region are closed as a precaution, with staff instructed to work remotely where possible. “We are assessing the full extent of the damage and coordinating with local authorities to ensure the well-being of our employees,” the spokesperson added.

The Spanish Banking Association said in a statement that dozens of banking sector employees have been temporarily relocated from affected sites, and some data processing facilities have experienced outages. “Business continuity plans are in effect, but the severity of the weather is presenting ongoing challenges,” said association president Javier Redondo.

Industry analysts warned that continued severe weather could further hamper day-to-day operations. “The banking sector’s own infrastructure is under significant strain,” said analyst Marta Palacios. “Recovery may take several days depending on the progression of the storm.”

Authorities have issued further weather warnings for much of central and eastern Spain, and banking firms are monitoring the situation closely as the storms continue.
